Also note the go directive vs toolchain directive distinction:
- go line: minimum required Go version; mandatory since 1.21; toolchains refuse to load modules declaring newer Go; also sets language version enforced by compiler; must be ≥ dependency go lines.
- toolchain line: suggested/preferred toolchain; only takes effect in the main module (or workspace), and only when the default toolchain is older than the suggestion. It is not a requirement enforced on downstream consumers of the module — since downstream builds use their own main module. Dependencies' toolchain lines are ignored when building a downstream module? Let's check: the doc says "Only takes effect when the module is the main module and the default toolchain is older than the suggested toolchain" (gomod-ref toolchain-notes). That's the key documented statement about downstream consumers. The toolchain line in a dependency is not consulted. However, a dependency's `go` line does propagate: "A module's go line must declare a version greater than or equal to the go version declared by each of the modules listed in require statements" — so if a dependency declares go 1.22.0, main module's go.mod must be ≥ 1.22.0, and commands like go get/go mod tidy maintain this; that can push consumers' go lines and thus their toolchain selection. Also go command may switch toolchains mid-command when a newly added module requires newer Go (go get, go work use, go work sync, go install pkg@version, go run pkg@version).

So the dependency suggestion (toolchain line) does NOT affect downstream consumers; the dependency's go line does propagate as a minimum requirement which can force a consumer to upgrade its own go line/toolchain.

Also worth noting: `toolchain default` disables automatic switching for that module (i.e., pins to default toolchain).

GOSUMDB=off: The doc explicitly states toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off — "Because the specific toolchain used depends on the system's own default toolchain as well as the local operating system and architecture (GOOS and GOARCH), it is not practical to write toolchain module checksums to go.sum. Instead, toolchain downloads fail for lack of verification if GOSUMDB=off." So the proposal is backwards: GOSUMDB=off does not make automatic toolchain downloads work; it makes them fail. Also GOPRIVATE and GONOSUMDB patterns do not apply to toolchain downloads. So can't exempt.

And the claim that +path makes the entire build network-free is wrong: +path only disables the toolchain download fallback. Module dependencies are still fetched via GOPROXY (unless vendored, GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor, or GOPROXY=off with module cache). Toolchain downloads are separate from module downloads. So +path does not establish network-free builds; to be network-free, you need toolchains preinstalled on PATH and module cache/vendor complete.

So for verified toolchains in restricted CI, preinstall exact toolchains and verify their hashes yourself; or allow GOPROXY access with default GOSUMDB=sum.golang.org for downloads.

Recommended policy: keep GOTOOLCHAIN=auto (or pin goX.Y.Z+auto with preinstalled toolchain) and leave GOSUMDB at default (sum.golang.org) if network allowed. For restricted CI: preinstall exact toolchains on PATH, set GOTOOLCHAIN=local + go line pinned to the bundled version (or goX.Y.Z+path with the toolchain on PATH), vendor dependencies and set GOFLAGS=-mod=vendor (or GOPROXY=off).
